title: Pupil's marked test paper and feedback
subject: English
unit: Summer 2: Biographies: conviction, justice and legacy
source: Seeded from english/y7 lesson 74 (Pupil's marked test paper and feedback (portal))
intro: Test. Answer every question in the spaces provided. Show your working: marks are given for method. The marks for each question are shown in brackets.

questions.q: Ali lost three and a half years of his career rather than go against his beliefs. What does this show?
questions.a: B) conviction. Giving up so much for a belief shows conviction: a firmly held principle guiding his actions.

questions.q: What is the writer's main viewpoint?
questions.a: C) Perseverance matters more than talent. The final sentences say perseverance, not giftedness, is the real question.

questions.q: What does 'unbroken' suggest about Ali?
questions.a: A) his spirit survived great pressure. Unbroken implies something that faced force but did not break: his will, not his body.

questions.q: Which is a precise DIRT improvement?
options: Add a Zoom in on 'unbroken' and explain its connotation
questions.a: B) Add a Zoom in on 'unbroken' and explain its connotation. A precise improvement names a specific skill to add.

questions.q: Why might a ruler of a huge state choose patched clothes?
options: because he had no money at all
to stay humble and close to ordinary people
questions.a: C) to stay humble and close to ordinary people. Choosing simplicity while holding power shows humility and solidarity with the people.

questions.q: Which sentence links best after: 'Umar asked governors to explain their wealth.'?
options: This shows he held others to the same standard he held himself.
Umar asked governors to explain their wealth.
questions.a: A) This shows he held others to the same standard he held himself.. 'This shows' uses a pronoun to refer back and develops the idea; the others repeat or break the link.

questions.q: complete the timeline with eight events and write two sentences on why each of two events matters
questions.a: An eight-event timeline with explanations
questions.model: I do first: 1964: he became world champion at 22 and announced he was a Muslim, which shows he was proud of his faith even at the height of fame.

questions.q: in the Biography Journal, record five significant events and five new words
questions.a: Five events and five words with definitions

questions.q: explain the difference between a biography and an autobiography, with an example of each feature
questions.a: Third person vs first person; written by others vs by the subject

questions.q: When and where did Ali win Olympic gold?
questions.a: 1960, in Rome
questions.model: I do: scan the timeline for Olympic: 1960, Rome.

questions.q: Why was Ali banned from boxing in 1967?
questions.a: he refused the military draft because of his religious beliefs

questions.q: in the portal response box, explain the writer's viewpoint and two methods. Starter: 'The writer believes that...'
questions.a: Viewpoint with two methods and effects
questions.model: Point: The writer believes perseverance matters more than talent. | Evidence: 'it is perseverance that walks through it' | Method: an extended metaphor of a door | Effect: makes the idea easy to picture; talent only starts, effort finishes

questions.q: write a comparison of the article and Ali's biography using 'Similarly' or 'Likewise'
questions.a: A two-sentence comparison

questions.q: do you agree? Give one reason for and one against
questions.a: For example: for: practice builds skill; against: some talents give a real head start

questions.q: Retrieve two examples the writer gives
questions.a: a pianist's practice; a scientist's failed experiments
questions.model: I do: scan for examples after 'look closely': a pianist, a scientist.

questions.q: What does 'unglamorous effort' mean?
questions.a: hard work that is not exciting or praised

questions.q: in the portal response box, write one PETZAAL paragraph: How does the writer present Ali's perseverance? Starter: 'The writer presents Ali as...'
questions.a: A full PETZAAL paragraph
questions.model: Point: The writer presents Ali as persevering. | Evidence: he 'returned to the ring, older but unbroken' | Technique: contrast | Zoom in: 'older' admits the cost; 'unbroken' denies defeat | Analyse: time took his youth, not his will | Alternative: some may see pride, not perseverance | Link: the comeback becomes the heart of his legacy

questions.q: add a second Zoom in on a different word
questions.a: A second word analysed

questions.q: write an Alternative that genuinely challenges your Point
questions.a: For example: a reader in 1967 might have called his refusal unpatriotic

questions.q: Embed this quotation: 'did not give way'
questions.a: For example: Despite losing his title, Ali 'did not give way'.
questions.model: I do: write my own sentence and slot the quotation in so it reads smoothly.

questions.q: Zoom in: what does 'stripped' suggest?
questions.a: his title was taken forcefully, leaving him exposed

questions.q: DIRT: improve your PETZAAL paragraph from lesson 64 using your feedback
questions.a: An improved paragraph with a visible change
questions.model: Before: 'Ali was strong because he came back.' | After: 'The phrase "older but unbroken" presents Ali's return as a victory of will: the ban took years, not his spirit.'
